posture: Inform — a quiet scan with one dated procedural milestone. Today marks the close of the public submission window (6 July–6 August) on EnergyCo's draft New England REZ Access Scheme Declaration, so the Minister for Energy now moves to consider submissions before deciding whether to formally declare the scheme; that milestone is logged below as the day's single item because, while flagged as context in prior digests, it has not been recorded as an item and its 6 August close date falls squarely in today's window. Every other live thread was captured in the 3 August digest and is deduplicated out: the NSW Legislative Council Portfolio Committee No. 4 final report (tabled 29 July — 25 findings, 16 recommendations, 'predictable and avoidable' harm, a specific finding that EnergyCo failed its central coordinating role, and a three-month clock to roughly end October for a government implementation plan with six-monthly reporting to Parliament); Upper Hunter Shire Council's 28 July call for the state to pause New England land acquisition; and EnergyCo's deferral of the New England (Muswellbrook–Armidale) aerial survey to September. No formal NSW Government response to the inquiry has yet surfaced. Two near-term milestones sit just ahead and are noted for situational awareness though each was previously logged and is not repeated as an item: ACEREZ opens Round 2 of its Central-West Orana community grants (~$1.9m) on 10 August, and EnergyCo runs its Central-West Orana community roadshow across 11–15 August. Paid mastheads (AFR, SMH and the ACM regional titles) surfaced only recycled coverage of the inquiry, corridor and grants stories at headline level and were not opened. Net: no new decision-grade or developing signal today; a single contextual milestone logged to keep the archive continuous.
summary: The only genuinely dated, not-previously-logged signal today is the 6 August close of public submissions on EnergyCo's draft New England REZ Access Scheme Declaration, which now passes to the Minister for Energy to weigh before any formal declaration. All other active threads — the upper-house inquiry's final report and its government-response clock, Upper Hunter Council's acquisition-pause call, and the deferred New England aerial survey — were captured in the 3 August digest and are deduplicated out, and no government response to the inquiry has appeared. Near-term milestones (ACEREZ Round 2 grants open 10 August; Central-West Orana roadshow 11–15 August) remain as previously logged.

items.headline: Public submissions close on EnergyCo's draft New England REZ Access Scheme Declaration
items.summary: The public consultation window on EnergyCo's draft New England REZ Access Scheme Declaration and positions paper, open from 6 July, closes today (6 August). The scheme sets the proposed rules for how generation and storage projects connect to New England transmission and how access is priced to fund community and employment benefits; the Minister for Energy will consider the submissions received before deciding whether to formally declare the scheme.
items.so_what: The submissions now form part of the record the Minister weighs, and — landing barely a week after the upper-house inquiry's finding that EnergyCo's consultation gave communities 'no meaningful influence' — the quality and tenor of this feedback is a live test of engagement credibility for the largest planned zone. Watch for the closing of the window to trigger the next decision point (a declaration or a revised paper) and for developer or landholder submissions to surface access-pricing or connection-sequencing concerns that could shape investment and delivery risk across New England.
